bill_text.text_with_changes:
A bill for an act relating to health care; regulating prepayments for certain dental services; amending Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 150A.11, by adding a subdivision.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 150A.11, is amended by adding a subdivision to read:

[+Subd. 5.+]

[+Prepayment for certain dental services.+]

[+For dental services in a dental treatment plan scheduled to take more than 90 days to complete, a dentist or dental practice is prohibited from requiring the patient to prepay any portion of the amount owed for the dental services before beginning to provide the dental services. Upon beginning to provide dental services to the patient according to a dental treatment plan scheduled to take more than 90 days to complete, a dentist or dental practice must allow the patient to pay for the dental services with at least two payments due at least 30 days apart. +]
bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to health care; regulating prepayments for certain dental services; amending Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 150A.11, by adding a subdivision.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 150A.11, is amended by adding a subdivision to read:

Subd. 5.

Prepayment for certain dental services.

For dental services in a dental treatment plan scheduled to take more than 90 days to complete, a dentist or dental practice is prohibited from requiring the patient to prepay any portion of the amount owed for the dental services before beginning to provide the dental services. Upon beginning to provide dental services to the patient according to a dental treatment plan scheduled to take more than 90 days to complete, a dentist or dental practice must allow the patient to pay for the dental services with at least two payments due at least 30 days apart.
additions: For dental services in a dental treatment plan scheduled to take more than 90 days to complete, a dentist or dental practice is prohibited from requiring the patient to prepay any portion of the amount owed for the dental services before beginning to provide the dental services. Upon beginning to provide dental services to the patient according to a dental treatment plan scheduled to take more than 90 days to complete, a dentist or dental practice must allow the patient to pay for the dental services with at least two payments due at least 30 days apart.
